That record lists si_dimension: L (unit m), so the only nonzero base dimension is length. Therefore the candidate SI exponent vector (L=1, all others 0) exactly matches the documented dimensionality and supports all known coordinates of the proposed vector.

The ledger defines kt as peak-to-valley height. The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height has canonical_quantity 'mean peak-to-valley roughness height' with symbols including kt and definition 'A roughness-amplitude measure formed from vertical height differences between peaks and valleys.' That record has si_dimension: L (unit m), so the candidate vector with length exponent 1 and all other exponents zero matches the KB definition and supports all known coordinates of the proposed SI vector.

The typed ledger gives k_rms as the root-mean-square height. The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height is canonical for 'root-mean-square roughness height' with symbols k_rms and definition 'Root-mean-square fluctuation of surface height about its mean.' The KB entry lists si_dimension: L (unit m), so the only nonzero exponent is length. The candidate vector (L=1, others 0) is therefore supported by this record and matches all known coordinates.

The ledger defines Sk as the third central moment normalized by cube of RMS (surface-height skewness). The KB record pq_height_skewness has canonical_quantity 'surface-height skewness' with symbols Sk and definition 'Third standardized moment of the surface-height distribution.' It explicitly lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). Thus the proposed SI exponent vector with all zeros is exactly supported by the cited record and covers all known coordinates of Sk's dimensionality.

Ku in the ledger is the kurtosis of height fluctuations. The KB record pq_height_kurtosis has canonical_quantity 'surface-height kurtosis' with symbols Ku and definition 'Fourth standardized moment of the surface-height distribution.' The KB entry lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). Therefore the candidate SI exponent vector of all zeros is confirmed by this record and supports all known coordinates of Ku's dimensionality.

The ledger defines ES as the effective streamwise slope (mean absolute surface slope). The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope has canonical_quantity 'effective surface slope' with symbols ES and definition 'Mean absolute gradient of surface height in a specified horizontal direction.' It states that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). Thus the candidate vector with all zeros (dimensionless) exactly matches the KB entry and supports all known coordinates of ES's dimensionality.

Po is given in the ledger as surface porosity. The KB record pq_porosity has canonical_quantity 'porosity' with symbols Po and definition 'Fraction of void or open volume/area' and lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). Therefore the all-zero SI exponent vector proposed for Po is supported by the cited KB record and covers all known coordinates of porosity's dimensionality.

Ku in the ledger is the kurtosis of height fluctuations. The KB record pq_height_kurtosis has canonical_quantity 'surface-height kurtosis' with symbols Ku and definition 'Fourth standardized moment of the surface-height distribution.' The KB entry lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). Therefore the candidate SI exponent vector of all zeros is confirmed by this record and supports all known coordinates of Ku's dimensionality.

The ledger defines ES as the effective streamwise slope (mean absolute surface slope). The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope has canonical_quantity 'effective surface slope' with symbols ES and definition 'Mean absolute gradient of surface height in a specified horizontal direction.' It states that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). Thus the candidate vector with all zeros (dimensionless) exactly matches the KB entry and supports all known coordinates of ES's dimensionality.

Po is given in the ledger as surface porosity.
